_comment: PLACEHOLDER: 4-channel kitchen timer. Every pan/tilt angle is null, fill them in on the rig (see firmware/README.md). One finger on pan/tilt: Pam presses with ANGLE 0, so servo 0 tilts (presses) and servo 1 pans. Control ids match vision/calibration/timer-01.boxes.json. Anything in the notes marked UNVERIFIED hasn't been checked on the real timer.
notes: Four channels, T1 to T4. Each has its own LCD row (screen_t1 to screen_t4) showing HH:MM SS, so 00:05 00 is 5 minutes.
The current screen above is a fixed starting point, not read from the camera, so a channel may already be running.
Press T1, T2, T3 or T4 to pick that channel. H, M, S, 10M, 5M, 10S, ST/SP and RESET act on the picked channel.
UNVERIFIED: what pressing T1 to T4 shows (a flashing row or digit), and which channel is picked after power-on.
Set the time with H, M and S. UNVERIFIED: each press adds 1 hour, 1 minute or 1 second, and what happens past 59 (or 23 hours).
10M, 5M and 10S are shortcuts. UNVERIFIED: each press adds 10 minutes, 5 minutes or 10 seconds to the time already set (rather than setting it to that value).
ST/SP starts the picked channel, or stops it if it is running.
UNVERIFIED: a started channel counts down from the set time (so 00:05 00 reads 00:04 59 a second later), and what it does at 00:00 00 (beeps, counts up).
To check a channel really started, expect the time it shows after it has started counting (for 5 minutes, expect 00:04), never the time that was set: that is on screen even if ST/SP did nothing.
UNVERIFIED: RESET clears to 00:00 00 (not back to the last set time), and whether it works on a running channel or needs ST/SP to stop it first.

Approval: the step that presses ST/SP gets requires_approval true with a reason (it starts or stops a channel). The step that presses RESET gets requires_approval true and destructive true: on a running channel it wipes the time someone is counting. Picking a channel or setting the time needs no approval.
